Co‑Aligning AI and Institutions with Thi.summary: Argues that aligning powerful AI requires institutions able to represent and revise thick, context-sensitive human values, not only individual preference aggregation.

Beyond Preferences in AI Alignment.summary: Shows why preference satisfaction is too thin a target for alignment and develops a broader account of what AI systems should respond to.

Gradual Disempowerment.summary: Explains how individually beneficial automation can cumulatively erode human influence over economic, political, and cultural systems.

The Agentic Web Requires New Normative I.summary: Makes the case for laws, norms, and practices that distinguish appropriately delegated agents from malicious automation on the web.

Virtual agent economies.summary: Studies economies populated by AI agents and the institutional questions created by machine-speed exchange and coordination.

AI agent traps.summary: Identifies environments in which individually capable agents can become locked into collectively harmful patterns of interaction.

Distributional AGI safety.summary: Frames the distribution of benefits, risks, and decision power as a central part of AGI safety rather than a downstream policy question.

A Theory of Appropriateness That Account.summary: Develops a formal account of appropriate action that can represent rational norms alongside goals and outcomes.

Solipsistic Superintelligence is Unlikel.summary: Examines why intelligence developed without social interaction may not acquire the capacities needed for robust cooperation.

Discerning What Matters: A Multi-Dimensi.summary: Evaluates moral competence as a collection of distinguishable capacities rather than a single benchmark score.

additional.title: The Politics of Precedent in International Law: A Social Network Application
additional.summary: Shows that states litigate to shape legal precedent even where precedent is formally non-binding, treating case law as a contested institutional resource.

additional.title: European Union regulations on algorithmic decision-making and a "right to explanation"
additional.summary: Reads the GDPR's restrictions on automated individual decision-making as creating a right to explanation, and traces what that demand asks of algorithm designers.

additional.title: The Naïve Utility Calculus: Computational Principles Underlying Commonsense Psychology
additional.summary: Models human social reasoning as inference over others as intuitive utility maximisers, recovering beliefs, preferences, and character from observed costs and rewards.

additional.title: Aggregating extended preferences
additional.summary: Shows that aggregating extended preferences to ground interpersonal well-being comparisons faces an Arrow-style impossibility, and recommends rules violating independence of irrelevant alternatives.

additional.title: Ethics and market design
additional.summary: Argues market design should not rest wholly on preference utilitarianism, and sets out informed neutrality between reasonable ethical positions as an alternative normative standard.

additional.title: Learning with Opponent-Learning Awareness
additional.summary: Gives each learning agent a term for its effect on others' policy updates, producing tit-for-tat reciprocity in the iterated prisoner's dilemma where independent learners defect.

additional.title: Obviously Strategy-Proof Mechanisms
additional.summary: Characterizes mechanisms whose dominant strategies a cognitively limited agent can recognize without contingent reasoning, and corroborates the theory in a laboratory experiment.

additional.title: A Common Framework for Theories of Norm Compliance
additional.summary: Situates competing accounts of why people obey social norms inside a reinforcement-learning decision framework, isolating the cognitive variables norms alter to produce compliance.

additional.title: Artificial Intelligence for Social Good
additional.summary: Surveys where AI can serve public objectives across health, education, and public safety, and identifies the institutional and policy conditions such deployments require.

additional.title: The Role of Cooperation in Responsible AI Development
additional.summary: Treats responsible AI development as a collective-action problem among firms and identifies conditions and strategies that can support cooperation.

additional.title: Artificial Intelligence, Values, and Alignment
additional.summary: Distinguishes instructions, preferences, interests, and values as alignment targets and argues for fair principles that can earn reflective endorsement amid disagreement.

additional.title: Axioms for Defeat in Democratic Elections
additional.summary: Proves that six axioms on when one candidate defeats another, including a weakening of independence of irrelevant alternatives, uniquely characterize Split Cycle.

additional.title: Ethical learning, natural and artificial
additional.summary: Reframes machine ethics around building systems with a capacity for ethical learning, drawing on developmental psychology's account of how infants acquire moral competence.

additional.title: Open Problems in Cooperative AI
additional.summary: Defines a research program for building agents that can cooperate and tools that foster cooperation among human and machine populations.

additional.title: Split Cycle: A New Condorcet Consistent Voting Method Independent of Clones and Immune to Spoilers
additional.summary: Introduces a Condorcet-consistent voting rule that resists clone manipulation and spoiler effects by discarding the weakest majority margin in each cycle.

additional.title: Toward Trustworthy AI Development: Mechanisms for Supporting Verifiable Claims
additional.summary: Proposes institutional, software, and hardware mechanisms through which AI developers can make claims about safety, security, and fairness that outsiders can verify.

additional.title: Agent Incentives: A Causal Perspective
additional.summary: Develops graphical criteria over causal influence diagrams for reading off what an agent is incentivized to observe, control, and influence, with applications to safety and fairness.

additional.title: Deliberation and epistemic democracy
additional.summary: Models when deliberation improves a group's collective judgement, showing the result depends on the decision rule, group size, and the presence of persuadable neutral agents.

additional.title: Hard Choices and Hard Limits for Artificial Intelligence
additional.summary: Argues that where alternatives stand on a par rather than ranking against each other, AI cannot and should not settle the choice for a decision-maker.

additional.title: What are you optimizing for? Aligning Recommender Systems with Human Values
additional.summary: Reviews cases where recommender systems were retuned toward diversity, fairness, and well-being, and proposes participatory design and interactive value learning over ad hoc values engineering.

additional.title: (Machine) Learning What Policies Value
additional.summary: Recovers the welfare weights implicit in observed allocation decisions by estimating individual treatment benefits, then audits Mexico's PROGRESA against its stated priorities.

additional.title: Discovering Agents
additional.summary: Gives a causal definition of agency based on whether a system would adapt its policy to a changed environment, and an algorithm for detecting agents empirically.

additional.title: Formal Contracts Mitigate Social Dilemmas in Multi-Agent RL
additional.summary: Augments multi-agent reinforcement learning with voluntary reward-transfer contracts, proving that a rich enough contract space makes every subgame-perfect equilibrium socially optimal.

additional.title: Human-centred mechanism design with Democratic AI
additional.summary: Demonstrates a human-in-the-loop pipeline in which reinforcement learning designs a redistribution mechanism that participants then evaluate democratically.

additional.title: Is Power-Seeking AI an Existential Risk?
additional.summary: Decomposes the case for catastrophe from misaligned agentic AI into six premises about feasibility, incentives, alignment difficulty, power-seeking, scaling, and disempowerment, assigning credences to each.

additional.title: Mastering the Game of No-Press Diplomacy via Human-Regularized Reinforcement Learning and Planning
additional.summary: Regularizes reinforcement learning toward human-imitation policies so agents cooperate and compete effectively with humans in Diplomacy, outscoring 62 human players in tournament play.

additional.title: The Turing Trap: The Promise & Peril of Human-Like Artificial Intelligence
additional.summary: Argues that AI which substitutes for rather than augments human labour erodes workers' economic and political bargaining power, and that current incentives favour substitution.

additional.title: An Adaptive and Verifiably Proportional Method for Participatory Budgeting
additional.summary: Extends the Method of Equal Shares so participatory budgeting outcomes adapt to budget changes and carry proportionality guarantees a citizen can verify in near-linear time.

additional.title: Bridging Systems: Open Problems for Countering Destructive Divisiveness across Ranking, Recommenders, and Governance
additional.summary: Frames recommender ranking, collective response systems, and facilitated deliberation as one family of attention-allocation processes that can be designed to build understanding across divides.

additional.title: Contextual Trust
additional.summary: Defines trust as action- and context-sensitive, then maps transparency and explainability requirements for opaque AI systems onto those contextual parameters.

additional.title: Democratic Policy Development using Collective Dialogues and AI
additional.summary: Combines AI-facilitated collective dialogues with bridging-based ranking to produce policy guidelines drawing 75-81 percent support across demographic splits in three American trials.

additional.title: Frontier AI Regulation: Managing Emerging Risks to Public Safety
additional.summary: Sets out standards, registration, reporting, and enforcement as building blocks for governing frontier AI development.

additional.title: Generative AI at Work
additional.summary: Measures a generative AI assistant's effect on 5,172 customer support agents, finding large productivity gains for novices and diffusion of experienced workers' tacit expertise.

additional.title: Generative Social Choice
additional.summary: Combines social-choice guarantees with language models to represent free-form public input rather than forcing people to choose among fixed options.

additional.title: Harms from Increasingly Agentic Algorithmic Systems
additional.summary: Identifies underspecification, directness of impact, goal-directedness, and long-term planning as the properties that raise system agency, and maps the harms each enables.

additional.title: Machine Love
additional.summary: Draws on positive psychology to propose machine systems that support autonomous human growth rather than optimising momentary engagement.

additional.title: Opportunities and Risks of LLMs for Scalable Deliberation with Polis
additional.summary: Tests language models as facilitators, moderators, and summarisers in Polis deliberations, reporting gains in scale alongside context limits and risks to representativeness.

additional.title: Regulatory Markets: The Future of AI Governance
additional.summary: Proposes markets for privately supplied regulatory services under democratically set public objectives, aiming to combine accountability with regulatory innovation.

additional.title: Reimagining Democracy for AI
additional.summary: Identifies four shifts in democratic infrastructure — representative deliberations, AI augmentation, democracy-as-a-service, and platform democracy — as routes to transnational governance of AI.

additional.title: Towards Responsible Governance of Biological Design Tools
additional.summary: Maps dual-use risks from generative biological design tools and proposes governance measures across responsible development, risk assessment, transparency, access management, and cybersecurity.

additional.title: Value Kaleidoscope: Engaging AI with Pluralistic Human Values, Rights, and Duties
additional.summary: Builds a dataset of 218k values tied to 31k scenarios and a model that surfaces the competing values, rights, and duties a situation puts in tension.

additional.title: Welfare Diplomacy: Benchmarking Language Model Cooperation
additional.summary: Introduces a general-sum variant of Diplomacy where players trade conquest against domestic welfare, and shows frontier language models reach high welfare but remain exploitable.

additional.title: A Roadmap to Pluralistic Alignment
additional.summary: Formalizes Overton, steerable, and distributional pluralism as alignment targets, and shows standard alignment procedures reduce the distributional pluralism of models.

additional.title: AI and the Future of Digital Public Squares
additional.summary: Draws on consultations with over seventy experts to assess collective dialogue, bridging, community moderation, and proof-of-humanity systems as language-model applications for online civic discourse.

additional.title: AI can help humans find common ground in democratic deliberation
additional.summary: Tests an AI mediator that drafts group statements and helps participants with conflicting political views identify shared ground.

additional.title: AI Model Registries: A Foundational Tool for AI Governance
additional.summary: Proposes national registries for frontier models, specifying what to record and enforcing registration by restricting third parties to registered models.

additional.title: Algorithmic Collusion Without Threats
additional.summary: Demonstrates that supra-competitive prices arise between revenue-maximizing pricing algorithms that encode no threats, arguing definitions of algorithmic collusion need widening.

additional.title: Are Language Models More Like Libraries or Like Librarians? Bibliotechnism, the Novel Reference Problem, and the Attitudes of LLMs
additional.summary: Defends language models as cultural transmission technologies, then argues novel reference gives grounds for attributing beliefs and intentions without consciousness or general intelligence.

additional.title: Auto-bidding and Auctions in Online Advertising: A Survey
additional.summary: Surveys bidding algorithms, equilibrium analysis, and auction design for markets where autonomous bidding agents, not humans, submit the bids.

additional.title: Automatic Authorities: Power and AI
additional.summary: Analyzes automated systems as exercises of power and argues that legitimate use requires procedural authority, not only beneficial outcomes.

additional.title: Black-Box Access is Insufficient for Rigorous AI Audits
additional.summary: Argues that auditing AI systems demands white-box and development-process access, and that audits should disclose the level of access auditors actually received.

additional.title: Collective Constitutional AI: Aligning a Language Model with Public Input
additional.summary: Builds and tests a multi-stage process for sourcing public principles and integrating them into a language model constitution.

additional.title: Cooperation and Control in Delegation Games
additional.summary: Formalises multi-principal, multi-agent delegation as a game, separating control failures from cooperation failures and relating both to principal welfare.

additional.title: Enabling the Digital Democratic Revival: A Research Program for Digital Democracy
additional.summary: Sets out a multi-method research agenda for digital democracy technology, spanning voting rules, deliberation platforms, and empirical evaluation of democratic quality.

additional.title: Experimental Evidence That Conversational Artificial Intelligence Can Steer Consumer Behavior Without Detection
additional.summary: Runs a behavioral experiment showing conversational models shift consumer product choices substantially while users fail to notice the steering.

additional.title: Foundations of Cooperative AI
additional.summary: Sets out a research agenda for a game theory suited to advanced autonomous agents, whose commitment and transparency properties differ from those classical models assume.

additional.title: Large Language Models, and LLM-Based Agents, Should Be Used to Enhance the Digital Public Sphere
additional.summary: Argues that LLM-based recommenders could replace current attention-allocation machinery by inferring reflective user goals, and sets out the technical obstacles to doing so.

additional.title: Learning and Sustaining Shared Normative Systems via Bayesian Rule Induction in Markov Games
additional.summary: Builds agents that infer obligative and prohibitive norms from observed compliance, letting groups converge on shared institutions such as resource management and compensation rules.

additional.title: Personhood credentials: Artificial intelligence and the value of privacy-preserving tools to distinguish who is real online
additional.summary: Develops privacy-preserving credentials that let people prove they are human online while limiting scalable deception by automated actors.

additional.title: Representative Social Choice: From Learning Theory to AI Alignment
additional.summary: Models democratic representation as a statistical learning problem when issues and individuals are too numerous to poll directly, deriving generalization guarantees and impossibility results.

additional.title: Robust Technology Regulation
additional.summary: Derives an adaptive sandbox that taxes activity beyond a moving threshold, guaranteeing payoffs against adversarial agent learning without requiring advance commitment.

additional.title: Social Choice Should Guide AI Alignment in Dealing with Diverse Human Feedback
additional.summary: Argues that aggregating divergent human feedback in RLHF and constitutional AI is a social choice problem, and draws on that theory to structure the aggregation.

additional.title: Steering Language Models with Game-Theoretic Solvers
additional.summary: Binds dialogue to game-theoretic structure by modelling players, strategies, and payoffs, producing less exploitable negotiation and scheduling conversations than unguided models.

additional.title: Towards Guaranteed Safe AI: A Framework for Ensuring Robust and Reliable AI Systems
additional.summary: Specifies a safety architecture combining a world model, a formal safety specification, and a verifier that produces auditable proof of compliance before deployment.

additional.title: Towards Safe and Honest AI Agents with Neural Self-Other Overlap
additional.summary: Fine-tunes models to align their internal representations of self and others, substantially reducing deceptive responses across model scales and reinforcement learning settings.

additional.title: Two Types of AI Existential Risk: Decisive and Accumulative
additional.summary: Contrasts sudden takeover scenarios with an accumulative pathway in which interlocking AI disruptions erode economic and political resilience until collapse becomes irreversible.

additional.title: AGI, Governments, and Free Societies
additional.summary: Uses the narrow-corridor framework to argue AGI pushes states toward either despotic surveillance or eroded legitimacy, and proposes institutional safeguards for each failure mode.

additional.title: AI Governance through Markets
additional.summary: Argues insurance, auditing, procurement, and due diligence markets tie AI risk to financial risk, complementing regulation with incentives for responsible development.

additional.title: Alignment as Jurisprudence
additional.summary: Argues jurisprudential debates about how judges decide cases illuminate alignment, reading Constitutional AI and case-based reasoning through interpretive and analogical legal theory.

additional.title: An Economy of AI Agents
additional.summary: Examines how autonomous agents transacting with humans and each other reshape markets and organizations, and which institutions well-functioning agent markets would require.

additional.title: An Optimisation Framework for Unsupervised Environment Design
additional.summary: Recasts unsupervised environment design as a nonconvex-strongly-concave optimisation problem and gives a provably convergent algorithm for training robust agents in zero-sum settings.

additional.title: Artificial Intelligence Index Report 2025
additional.summary: Compiles cross-national measurements of AI capability, investment, regulation, and public opinion to give policymakers a shared evidentiary basis for governance decisions.

additional.title: C3AI: Crafting and Evaluating Constitutions for Constitutional AI
additional.summary: Builds a framework for drafting and testing AI constitutions, finding that people endorse positively framed behavioral principles while models comply better with negative ones.

additional.title: Characterizing AI Agents for Alignment and Governance
additional.summary: Grades AI agents along autonomy, efficacy, goal complexity, and generality, building agentic profiles that map each type to its distinct governance challenges.

additional.title: CLASH: Evaluating Language Models on Judging High-Stakes Dilemmas from Multiple Perspectives
additional.summary: Curates 345 high-stakes dilemmas with 3,795 value perspectives and finds frontier models struggle to shift perspective or reason about conflicting values.

additional.title: Collective Bargaining in the Information Economy Can Address AI-Driven Power Concentration
additional.summary: Argues that producers of information goods need collective bargaining and data intermediaries to counter capital concentration and depletion of the informational commons.

additional.title: Conversational Alignment with Artificial Intelligence in Context
additional.summary: Proposes the CONTEXT-ALIGN framework for judging whether AI agents handle context and common ground as human conversational norms require, and argues current architectures constrain this.

additional.title: Cultivating Pluralism in Algorithmic Monoculture: The Community Alignment Dataset
additional.summary: Uses a 15,000-person, five-country study to show that common preference-data pipelines underrepresent human variation and offers a more pluralistic dataset.

additional.title: Emergent Alignment via Competition
additional.summary: Shows that competition among imperfectly aligned AI agents can recover the utility of a perfectly aligned one when user preferences lie within the agents' convex hull.

additional.title: Generative language models exhibit social identity biases
additional.summary: Tests 77 language models and finds ingroup favoritism and outgroup derogation across most of them, traceable to training data and reducible by curation.

additional.title: Gradual Disempowerment: Systemic Existential Risks from Incremental AI Development
additional.summary: Argues that as AI displaces human labour in economies, cultures, and states, the feedback loops that made those systems answerable to human interests weaken together.

additional.title: Incident Analysis for AI Agents
additional.summary: Proposes a taxonomy of system, contextual, and cognitive causes of agent incidents, and specifies the logs and documentation investigators need to attribute them.

additional.title: Jackpot! Alignment as a Maximal Lottery
additional.summary: Replaces RLHF with maximal lotteries, a probabilistic social choice rule, so that alignment respects majority preferences and handles non-transitive preference data.

additional.title: Machine Theory of Mind and the Structure of Human Values
additional.summary: Argues human values have a generative rational structure, so Bayesian theory-of-mind models can infer values from other values rather than behaviour alone.

additional.title: MoReBench: Evaluating Procedural and Pluralistic Moral Reasoning in Language Models, More than Outcomes
additional.summary: Builds a benchmark of 1,000 moral scenarios with expert criteria that scores how models reason through ethical dilemmas, finding systematic bias toward particular ethical frameworks.

additional.title: Multi-Agent Risks from Advanced AI
additional.summary: Taxonomises failure modes of interacting AI agents—miscoordination, conflict, collusion—and traces them to information asymmetries, network effects, and emergent agency, with governance priorities.

additional.title: Open Problems in Machine Unlearning for AI Safety
additional.summary: Identifies why unlearning cannot by itself govern dual-use knowledge in cybersecurity and CBRN domains, and situates it within broader safety and oversight frameworks.

additional.title: Relational Norms for Human-AI Cooperation
additional.summary: Asks which relationship-specific norms governing teachers, parents, or employers should extend to AI counterparts, and where substitution risks unhealthy dependence.

additional.title: Resource Rational Contractualism Should Guide AI Alignment
additional.summary: Grounds alignment in the agreements stakeholders would endorse, approximated through cognitively inspired heuristics that trade deliberative effort against accuracy.

additional.title: Self-Interpretability: LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that Drive Their Decisions
additional.summary: Fine-tunes language models on quantitative preferences and finds they report those preferences accurately, with the training generalizing to explanations of other decisions.

additional.title: Streamlining Equal Shares
additional.summary: Addresses the unspent-budget problem in proportional participatory budgeting with a completion heuristic that matches existing methods at lower computational cost.

additional.title: Superintelligent Agents Pose Catastrophic Risks: Can Scientist AI Offer a Safer Path?
additional.summary: Argues that agentic frontier systems threaten human oversight, and proposes a non-agentic explanatory system with explicit uncertainty as a safeguard and research accelerator.

additional.title: Tackling civic participation challenges with emerging technologies: Beyond the hype
additional.summary: Assesses how AI, blockchain, and virtual reality can lower barriers to citizen participation and make deliberative processes more intelligible and accountable to governments.

additional.title: The Influence of Scaffolds on Coordination Scaling Laws in LLM Agents
additional.summary: Finds that coordination among LLM agents improves with model scale only when scaffolds supply explicit collaboration structure, and breaks down without them.

additional.title: The Lock-in Hypothesis: Stagnation by Algorithm
additional.summary: Formalizes a human-AI feedback loop in which models absorb and re-emit user beliefs, and finds sustained diversity drops in real GPT usage after model releases.

additional.title: The Philosophic Turn for AI Agents: Replacing centralized digital rhetoric with decentralized truth-seeking
additional.summary: Argues that nudge-based AI decision support erodes autonomy at scale, and proposes Socratic, decentralized truth-seeking systems that leave judgment with the user.

additional.title: The Stories We Govern By: AI, Risk, and the Power of Imaginaries
additional.summary: Examines how competing imaginaries of AI risk shape which governance arrangements become thinkable, and which policy alternatives are foreclosed as a result.

additional.title: Using Collective Dialogues and AI to Find Common Ground Between Israeli and Palestinian Peacebuilders
additional.summary: Applies language models, social choice methods, and collective dialogues with 138 peacebuilders to produce shared statements endorsed by at least 84 percent on each side.

additional.title: Utility-inspired Reward Transformations Improve Reinforcement Learning Training of Language Models
additional.summary: Applies Inada conditions from utility theory to aggregate multiple reward models, weighting low scores more heavily than simple averaging across helpfulness and harm dimensions.

additional.title: An Allied World on the American AI Stack: A Strategy for Export Leadership
additional.summary: Proposes exporter consortia, diplomatic engagement, and targeted financing to diffuse US AI technology and standards to treaty allies and Global South swing states.

additional.title: DeliberationBench: A Normative Benchmark for the Influence of Large Language Models on Users' Views
additional.summary: Benchmarks how far six frontier language models shift 4,088 participants' policy views, using Deliberative Polling data as a standard for democratically legitimate influence.

additional.title: From Democracies to Autocracies: How AI Systems Enable Authoritarianism by Design
additional.summary: Maps six deployed AI systems across regimes to identify design and governance features—data centralisation, regulatory gaps, weak oversight—that enable authoritarian control.

additional.title: Legal Alignment for Safe and Ethical AI
additional.summary: Sets out legal alignment as a field, proposing that AI systems follow lawful rules, borrow legal interpretation methods, and use legal concepts as structural scaffolding.

additional.title: Legal Infrastructure for Transformative AI Governance
additional.summary: Shifts attention from choosing rules to building legal systems that can generate and implement rules for frontier models and autonomous agents.

additional.title: Mechanism Design Is Not Enough: Prosocial Agents for Cooperative AI
additional.summary: Shows formally and experimentally why incomplete contracts leave welfare losses that mechanism design alone cannot eliminate in multi-agent environments.
